title: Reproducing David et al. 2015: germanium condensation under a dry oxide

sample.paper: “a 1µm thick Si0.8Ge0.2 relaxed layer on a graded SiGe buffer layer epitaxially grown on silicon”; graded buffer 5 µm (Figure 1 label)
sample.ours: FAMILY: SiGe_oxide; COMPOSITION: Si0.80Ge0.20; FILM recorded, read by no program
sample.note: Every program treats the alloy as infinite; for 1 µm that is fair.

sample.paper: “a 34 nm thick layer of Si0.8Ge0.2 deposited by molecular beam epitaxy (MBE) at 450 ◦C on an ultra-thin silicon on insulator (UTSOI)”; top Si 12 nm, BOX 10 nm; “fully strained”
sample.ours: COMPOSITION: Si0.80Ge0.20; FILM recorded, read by no program
sample.note: No program knows the alloy is 34 nm thick, that silicon lies under it, or that it is strained. After 6 h the alloy is gone and our programs keep oxidizing an infinite Si0.8Ge0.2.

sample.ours: ORIENTATION: Si100 on structure 2; none on structure 1

sample.paper: not stated (no clean, no native oxide)
sample.ours: CLEAN: not_stated; each program's own starting oxide

history.item: Graded SiGe buffer and 1 µm relaxed Si0.8Ge0.2, epitaxial
history.paper: “a 1µm thick Si0.8Ge0.2 relaxed layer on a graded SiGe buffer layer epitaxially grown on silicon”
history.ours: COMPOSITION on the sample; the layer stack is recorded (FILM) and read by no program

history.item: Into the JIPELEC rapid thermal oxidation furnace
history.paper: “rapid thermal oxidation (RTO) furnace JIPELEC”; nothing on cleaning, native oxide or storage before oxidation

history.ours: RUN RampUp DURATION 60 TEMP 25->750 AMBIENT dry_O2
history.note: One minute from room temperature, in oxygen. The ramp rate and the gas during the ramp are not stated.

history.paper: “The samples are oxidized for 90 min at various temperatures ranging from 700 ◦C to 950 ◦C.”
history.ours: RUN Oxidation DURATION 5400 TEMP 750->750 AMBIENT dry_O2
history.note: Oxygen at 1 atm assumed; flow and pressure are not stated.

history.ours: RUN RampDown DURATION 120 TEMP 750->300 AMBIENT dry_O2
history.note: A straight fall to 300 °C in two minutes, in oxygen; below 300 °C nothing in our programs moves.

history.item: Cross section by FIB, or tripod polishing and ion thinning
history.paper: “Cross section samples are prepared using a dual-beam FIB HELIOS 600 nanolab or tripod polishing followed by PIPS thinning.”
“The germanium concentration profiles were measured by STEM-EDS semi-quantitative analysis on the TEM cross section samples”
history.note: How the GRL edge and the oxide thickness were taken from the images is not stated.

history.paper: “part of germanium has been lost during the process (less than 10 %) by oxidation (formation of GeO2)”
history.ours: the inventory program conserves germanium exactly
